sentences.text: Gregory S. Paul estimated the animal measured 4 meters long and weighed 200 kilograms in 2010.
Thomas R. Holtz Jr. later suggested a length of 6.2 meters in 2012.
Molina-Pérez & Larramendi estimated the length at 8.5 meters and weight at 600 kilograms in 2016 based on specimen MNN TIG6.
Fossils were excavated in 1959 near Oued Timmersöi in the Agadez desert of Niger.
In 1960, Albert-Félix de Lapparent named the specimen as a second species of Elaphrosaurus.
The genus Spinostropheus was named in 2004 by Paul Sereno, Jeffrey A. Wilson, and John Conrad.
The generic name refers to prominent, dorso-ventrally flattened epipophyseal processes on the cervical vertebrae.
A 2002 analysis by Sereno et al. found Spinostropheus to be the sister taxon of Abelisauria.
Subsequent studies recovered it as a basal ceratosaur outside Neoceratosauria, closely related to Elaphrosaurus.
Carrano et al. (2012) classified the taxon as a basal Tetanuran.
Spinostropheus is classified within the infraorder Ceratosauria.
Spinostropheus lived during the Middle Jurassic in the Tiourarén Formation of Niger.
The Paleobiology Database lists the time range as Oxfordian to Cenomanian (161.5 to 93.9 million years ago).
Rauhut and Carrano (2016) suggested Spinostropheus might be a basal tetanuran because the holotype and paratypes lack ceratosaurian features found in specimen MNN TIG6.
